docs.explain: Three functions change case and nothing else. UPPER makes every letter a capital, LOWER drops them all, and PROPER capitalises the first letter of each word, which is what a name typed in capitals on a phone needs to read normally. PROPER decides where a word starts from punctuation, so it also capitalises after a dash, which is why the shipping label uses UPPER. None of them trims spaces or fixes spelling, so a name with two spaces between the words still reads oddly after PROPER. The conversion only goes one way: UPPER cannot tell you what the original was, so run these on a copy when the source spelling might matter later, such as a customer's name.

errors.text: The converted text was used in arithmetic, as in =UPPER(B7)/0.
UPPER was typed with an extra letter, which is a function the sheet has never heard of.

docs.atWork: Names and codes arriving from three systems, each of which shouts or whispers them.
